description:
Unsupervised, single-shot spike sorting for a 32-channel, 10 s extracellular recording. Steps:
- Common-average referencing (subtract per-sample median across channels) and robust per-channel noise estimation via MAD to get sigma.
- Negative threshold detection on each channel using robust threshold (4.5·sigma), local-minimum selection with per-channel refractory (12 samples ≈ 0.375 ms).
- Cross-channel deduplication: merge candidate peaks within ±12 samples across all channels, keep the most negative trough as a single event and record its primary channel and amplitude.
- Discard events too close to recording edges for waveform extraction.
- Geometry-aware feature extraction: for each event, take 8 nearest channels by electrode geometry, extract 48-sample snippets (0.5 ms pre, 1.0 ms post), whiten by per-channel sigma, flatten, and compute low-dimensional features using PCA (8 components) learned on an evenly spaced subset (up to 5000 events). Concatenate a normalized amplitude feature.
- Robust feature scaling (median/MAD) and clustering with KMeans using a heuristic K (3–16 depending on spike count). Discard tiny clusters.
- Template merging: build per-cluster mean templates across all 32 channels from up to 150 events/cluster (whitened). Merge clusters whose template cosine similarity > 0.95 and with primary channels within 65 µm (union-find).
- Enforce intra-unit refractory: within each unit, allow at most one spike per 12 samples, keeping the more negative amplitude event.
- Return integer array [sample_index, unit_id], sorted by sample then unit, with contiguous nonnegative unit IDs. No supervision, deterministic seeds, no ground-truth use.
Validation policy: purely unsupervised on the full 10 s recording; no use of any hidden labels/true unit counts/templates. Parameters chosen conservatively for generality and speed on a single CPU thread. No duplicate events within a unit are emitted; empty output is valid if no spikes are detected.
